plain: A European king named Frederick, who ruled lands in Bohemia and the Palatinate, is said to have sheltered a group of mystical and heretical thinkers, among them the English magician and scholar John Dee, his partner Edward Kelley, and possibly the philosopher Giordano Bruno. Michels takes this from the book The Rosicrucian Enlightenment by the historian Frances Yates, and adds, hedging with "I think", that when war came the philosopher René Descartes fought on the opposing side. He tells it to suggest that the rise of modern rational thought was bound up with a clash against these mystical circles.
